general-knowledge.title: General Knowledge
general-knowledge.description: Test your overall knowledge with a mix of questions.

questions.question: What is the capital of France?
questions.explanation: Paris is the capital and largest city of France.

questions.question: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.explanation: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa during the Renaissance.

questions.question: What is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system.

questions.question: In which year did World War II end?
questions.explanation: World War II ended in 1945 with Germany's surrender in May and Japan's surrender in August.

questions.question: What is the smallest country in the world?
questions.explanation: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world, with an area of 0.17 square miles.

questions.question: What is the most spoken language in the world?
questions.explanation: Mandarin Chinese is the most spoken language in the world by number of native speakers.

questions.question: Who is the author of 'Harry Potter'?
questions.explanation: J.K. Rowling is the author of the Harry Potter book series.

questions.question: What is the currency of Japan?
questions.explanation: The Yen is the official currency of Japan.

questions.question: How many continents are there?
questions.explanation: There are 7 continents: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, and Oceania.

questions.question: What is the tallest mountain in the world?
questions.explanation: Mount Everest is the tallest mountain in the world with a height of 29,032 feet (8,849 meters).

science.title: Science
science.description: Explore the wonders of science from biology to physics.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.explanation: Au is the chemical symbol for gold, derived from its Latin name 'aurum'.

questions.question: How many bones are in the human body?
questions.explanation: An adult human body has 206 bones. Babies are born with around 270 bones, but many fuse together as they grow.

questions.question: What is the process by which plants make their own food?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is the process where plants use sunlight to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen.

questions.question: What is the speed of light?
questions.explanation: The speed of light is approximately 300,000 kilometers per second (299,792 km/s to be precise).

questions.question: What is the study of rocks called?
questions.explanation: Geology is the science that studies the Earth, including rocks, minerals, and natural processes.

questions.question: What percentage of the Earth's atmosphere is oxygen?
questions.explanation: Approximately 21% of Earth's atmosphere is oxygen, while nitrogen makes up about 78%.

questions.question: What is the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: The mitochondria is known as the powerhouse of the cell because it produces energy in the form of ATP.

questions.question: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.explanation: The human heart has 4 chambers: two atria and two ventricles.

questions.question: What is the most abundant element in the universe?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe, making up about 75% of all baryonic mass.

questions.question: What type of animal is a dolphin?
questions.explanation: A dolphin is a mammal, despite living in water. Mammals have hair, warm blood, and nurse their young with milk.

history.title: History
history.description: Journey through time and learn about historical events.

questions.question: In which year did the Titanic sink?
questions.explanation: The RMS Titanic sank on April 15, 1912, after hitting an iceberg in the North Atlantic Ocean.

questions.question: Who was the first President of the United States?
questions.explanation: George Washington was the first President of the United States, serving from 1789 to 1797.

questions.question: What ancient wonder of the world still stands today?
questions.explanation: The Great Pyramid of Giza is the only surviving wonder of the ancient world.

questions.question: In which year did Christopher Columbus reach the Americas?
questions.explanation: Christopher Columbus reached the Americas on October 12, 1492, initiating sustained European exploration of the America.

questions.question: Who was the first Emperor of Rome?
questions.explanation: Augustus (Octavian) was the first Emperor of Rome, ruling from 27 BC to 14 AD.

questions.question: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
questions.explanation: The Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989, symbolizing the end of the Cold War and leading to German reunification.

questions.question: Who wrote the American Declaration of Independence?
questions.explanation: Thomas Jefferson was the primary author of the Declaration of Independence, adopted on July 4, 1776.

questions.question: In which century did the Renaissance occur?
questions.explanation: The Renaissance occurred primarily from the 14th to the 17th centuries, beginning in Italy and spreading across Europe.

questions.question: Who was the leader of Nazi Germany during World War II?
questions.explanation: Adolf Hitler was the Führer (leader) of Nazi Germany from 1933 until his death in 1945.

questions.question: In which year did the French Revolution begin?
questions.explanation: The French Revolution began in 1789, marked by the storming of the Bastille on July 14, 1789.

literature.title: Literature
literature.description: Discover the world of books and authors.

questions.question: Who wrote 'Pride and Prejudice'?
questions.explanation: Jane Austen wrote 'Pride and Prejudice', published in 1813, one of the most famous novels in English literature.

questions.question: What is the real name of the author George Orwell?
questions.explanation: George Orwell's real name was Eric Arthur Blair. He adopted the pen name 'George Orwell' for his writing.

questions.question: Who wrote 'The Great Gatsby'?
questions.explanation: F. Scott Fitzgerald wrote 'The Great Gatsby', published in 1925, a masterpiece of American literature.

questions.question: Which Shakespeare play features the character Hamlet?
questions.explanation: Hamlet is the protagonist and title character of Shakespeare's tragedy 'Hamlet, Prince of Denmark'.

questions.question: Who wrote 'One Hundred Years of Solitude'?
questions.explanation: Gabriel García Márquez wrote 'One Hundred Years of Solitude', a seminal work of magical realism published in 1967.

questions.question: What is the first book in the 'A Song of Ice and Fire' series?
questions.explanation: 'A Game of Thrones' is the first book in George R.R. Martin's 'A Song of Ice and Fire' series.

questions.question: Who wrote 'Jane Eyre'?
questions.explanation: Charlotte Brontë wrote 'Jane Eyre', published in 1847 under the pseudonym 'Currer Bell'.

questions.question: What is the genre of 'Moby Dick'?
questions.explanation: 'Moby Dick' by Herman Melville is an adventure novel and epic tale of a whaling ship's quest.

questions.question: Who wrote 'To Kill a Mockingbird'?
questions.explanation: Harper Lee wrote 'To Kill a Mockingbird', published in 1960, which won the Pulitzer Prize.

questions.question: What is the first book in the Harry Potter series?
options: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire
questions.explanation: 'Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone' (or 'Sorcerer's Stone' in the US) is the first book by J.K. Rowling.

mathematics.title: Mathematics
mathematics.description: Challenge your math skills with various problems.

questions.question: What is the value of π (pi) approximately?
questions.explanation: The value of π (pi) is approximately 3.14159, often rounded to 3.14.

questions.question: What is the square root of 144?
questions.explanation: The square root of 144 is 12 because 12 × 12 = 144.

questions.question: What is the result of 15 × 12?
What is the Fibonacci sequence's next number after 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8?
questions.explanation: The next number in the Fibonacci sequence is 13 (8 + 5 = 13). Each number is the sum of the two preceding ones.

questions.question: What is the area of a circle with radius 5?
questions.explanation: The area of a circle is πr². With r=5, area = π × 5² = 25π ≈ 78.5

questions.question: What is 25% of 200?
What is the sum of angles in a triangle?
questions.explanation: The sum of all angles in any triangle is always 180 degrees.

questions.question: What is the cube root of 27?
questions.explanation: The cube root of 27 is 3 because 3 × 3 × 3 = 27.

questions.question: What is 2⁶ (2 to the power of 6)?
What is the median of the numbers 3, 7, 9, 15, 20?
questions.explanation: The median is the middle value when numbers are arranged in order. In 3, 7, 9, 15, 20, the median is 9.
